title: Heavy rain likely in Odisha for 2 days, Orange alert for 6 districts - ODISHA RAY
article_text:
Bhubaneswar : Odisha is bracing for another spell of heavy rainfall as a cyclonic circulation over south Gangetic West Bengal and adjoining Bangladesh is likely to develop into a low-pressure area over Gangetic West Bengal and northwest Bay of Bengal.

The weather system is expected to bring heavy to very heavy rain for the next 2 days, with rainfall likely to continue for up to 5 days.

The weather department has issued an Orange warning for Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Sambalpur, Sundargarh, Jharsuguda and Bargarh. Eleven other districts are under Yellow warning.

The department has also warned of rough sea conditions. Wind speed may reach 40-50 kmph with gusts up to 60 kmph.



Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea on August 7 and 8 .

title: IMD predicts severe heatwave conditions over North, West India; heavy rainfall in NE region - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heat wave to severe heat wave conditions over West Madhya Pradesh and West Rajasthan for the next two days. East Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra are expected to reel under heat wave conditions tomorrow. The Weather agency also predicted heavy to very heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Meghalaya tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy rainfall is also likely over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Kerala, Mahe, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, Sub Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal during the next three days. Places over Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Chandigarh, Odisha, West Bengal and the Northeastern states are expected to experience thunderstorms and lightning tomorrow. According to the Met department, thundersquall conditions are expected during the next 2 days over Jharkhand, Coastal Karnataka, and North Interior Karnataka.

IMD further said that conditions are becoming favourable for the advance of southwest monsoon over parts of south Bay of Bengal, Andaman Sea and Andaman and Nicobar Islands around Saturday.

title: Alert issued for very heavy rain in Odisha - News On AIR
article_text:
Even as flood-hit people across Odisha are struggling to recover from the extensive damage caused by the recent floods, another spell of heavy rain is threatening to compound their woes.

The India Meteorological Department has issued a Red Warning for the state, forecasting widespread heavy to very heavy rain over the next 24 hours, with heavy rainfall likely to continue for three days.

The Salandi and Jalaka rivers are flowing above danger levels, posing fresh flood threats to Mayurbhanj, Balasore, Bhadrak and Keonjhar districts. An upper-air cyclonic circulation over south Gangetic West Bengal and adjoining Bangladesh is likely to trigger the formation of a low-pressure area over the coastal region and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal.

title: IMD predicts extremely heavy rainfall over Assam and Meghalaya tomorrow - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over Assam and Meghalaya for tomorrow. Heavy rainfall is also expected over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, and parts of North East India during the next two days. Similar weather conditions are expected over Kerala, Mahe, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Uttar Pradesh during the next two to three days.

The Met Department also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Jammu-Kashmir, Andhra Pradesh, Karaikal, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Odisha, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.

Meanwhile parts of Delhi witnessed rainfall today. The IMD predicted a generally cloudy sky with a spell of moderate rain at a few places of the national capital during early morning tomorrow. According to the Weather Agency, the maximum temperature will be around 32 to 34 degrees Celsius in Delhi while the minimum temperature will hover around 23 to 25 degrees Celsius tomorrow.

title: IMD Forecasts Heavy to Very Heavy Rainfall in Northeast; Heatwave Conditions Likely in Parts of West India - News On AIR
article_text:
India Meteorological Department has forecast fairly widespread to widespread rainfall along with thunderstorm, lightning and gusty winds with heavy to very heavy rainfall likely over Sub Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim and northeast India during the week. Isolated extremely heavy rainfall was witnessed over Assam and Meghalaya and Sub Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim today.

Maximum temperatures were in the range of 40 to 46 degree Celsius over most parts of the country except western Himalayan region, northeast Bihar, and northeast India, where they were below 36 degrees. The highest maximum temperature of 45.6 degrees was reported at Banda in Uttar Pradesh.

Isolated to scattered light to moderate rainfall with thunderstorm, lightning and gusty winds are likely over Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi tomorrow and during 2nd to 5th May. Meanwhile, heat wave conditions very likely in some places of Vidarbha today and in West Rajasthan during 1st to 3rd May. Hot and humid weather conditions are very likely to prevail in isolated pockets over Odisha from today till 1st May.
